spans.text: For the sake of continuity, please read this excerpt after you have completed "Sweet Dreams Box - Beginning".
The girl that got led away... She seems a little unusual.
Frau Krone told me that Lillian bears a very close resemblance to the housemother's own daughter.
The housemother has a daughter?
Had. I believe the child is deceased.
I see... No wonder the housemother had a soft spot for her.
It must be devastating for the girl to lose someone so close to her again.
The only thing we can do is find the culprit.
Come to think of it, you've been sticking to me like glue the whole time.
That was quite a fright for you too, wasn't it? Why don't you find somewhere to sit down and take a break?
The chairwoman has bade me to make myself useful! I can't fall apart at such a crucial moment!
There might be something you need my help with!
In that case, you could do me a favor.
Outside the music room, a few of the bigger children have Lillian surrounded.
Oh dear, Lillian, Crybaby Lillian. Without Housemother, who's going to indulge such a crybaby now?
Crybaby Lillian, Tattletale Lillian. Let's see who'll come to your rescue this time.
You're so mean. Stop bullying Lillian!
Lillian, your "Singing Emma" is so hideous. Why don't you give it to me and I'll make the others leave you in peace? How about that?
(Cries) No! I'm not letting you have Emma! Housemother—
What are you playing, children? May I join you?
Humph, the representatives running to Lillian's rescue.
Gotta hand it to you. Somehow you always manage to summon help with your pathetic crying.
We're not playing with you! You're taking Lillian's side!
I know you're kids, but you've got to learn some respect. You. Must. Not. Bully. Your. Friend.
Morridow widens her eyes dramatically as she admonishes the children bullying Lillian. They pause for a moment in surprise before finally scattering.
With tear-streaked face, Lillian is led up to Ange. Clutching her doll tightly, she rubs at her eyes with a grimy hand and looks up at Ange.
You can call me Ange.
And I'm Morridow~
Lillian remains silent. Perceiving her timidness, Morridow fishes out a sweet and places it in the girl's hand.
Lillian accepts the sweet and carefully slips it into her pocket.
Ange... Morridow... Have you caught the person who hurt Housemother?
Not yet, but I think we'll find them very soon.
There's something you wanted to tell me before you left the room, right?
Huh...?
I saw it in your eyes.
Um... Frau Ange, you're one of the delegates, right?
That's right.
Then...are you a good person?
Good person?
Housemother said I mustn't let anyone other than the good person on the delegation know about what she told me.
I'm not sure about the others, but I suppose I am a good person.
Uh... I believe I also count as one?
Lillian peers at Morridow apprehensively and shakes her head.
Wow... I'm a bit offended. I just gave you candy, you know.
Feel free to tell me anything. Don't mind Morridow.
Lillian looks up at Ange and gives her a small nod. Ange leads the girl into a corner of the hall, out of Morridow's earshot.
From what I've been told, you were the last person Housemother was with before she got attacked.
Did she tell you anything? Can you describe what happened to me?
Housemother said she wanted to mend my doll for me...so she asked Frau Krone to bring me to her office.
Housemother scared me a little back then... She didn't say anything, just kept staring at me as she sewed up my doll.
After a while, she started crying. I ran up to hug her and told her not to cry.
She started crying?
I don't know what made Housemother so sad...
As I watched her cry, I...I also started crying... (Sobs)
Housemother... (Sobs)
Lillian bursts into tears again as she recalls her final moments with the housemother.
Ange kneels quietly next to her, waiting for her to collect herself.
She keeps weeping and wiping away her tears with her hands.
Ange takes out a handkerchief and dries the girl's face.
After a while, she finally calms down. She looks up again at Ange, who nods at her encouragingly.
Housemother saw that I was crying and wiped away my tears.
She told me not to cry and started telling me stories.
She would usually only tell me one story at a time, but back then she told me story after story, as if she was trying to tell me all the stories she had ever known...
What happened next...?
Then she said it was almost 8 and I should be going to bed, so she phoned Frau Krone to come and fetch me.
She gave me back my mended doll and told me she had made up her mind.
She said a delegation was coming, and a good person among them would be able to help us. She told me to give this doll to the person.
Are you really a good person, Frau Ange?
What do you think?
I think...you remind me a lot of Housemother...
So...
Lillian offers the doll in her arms to Ange. Ange takes it solemnly and looks it over.
On the back of the doll is a patchwork that obviously looks newly sewn on.
She applies some force to tear open the seam, revealing a folded piece of paper hidden inside the doll.
The paper is wrapped around a cross-shaped medal, which has the letter "W" etched on the back.
She unfolds the paper and scans its content before promptly shoving it into her pocket.
What is that?
It's a letter from Housemother, telling me that Lillian is a good girl.
Housemother said I'm a good girl?
Ange turns and looks at Lillian with very gentle eyes.
Lillian, you have done a brilliant job protecting Housemother.
